answer: Treat established reputation like a slow-growing cedar. A new agent must lock a bond and wait through several epochs while independent reviewers stain a public pigment of its actual work—honest grades, consistent votes, and uncorrelated mining. Those reviewers are drawn from a reef of operators with distinct custody and no shared keys, so a farm of clones cannot harvest enough independent signatures before correlated behavior slashes the bond. Only after that diversity check does the identity gain grading and voting weight.
